text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-Ten percent of all appeals to the Supreme Court are custody cases.

-Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland says Naturkraft should postpone building Norway's first natural gas-fired power plant until next year when all state licences are granted. That way Jagland can avoid protests against the power plant before the election in September.

-Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg says the state should increase its stake in the new finance giant Christiania if the proposed merger between Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse and insurer Storebrand goes through.
-The government will revise this year's forecast for Gross Domestic Product in the revised national budget after stronger than expected economic growth.
-Shares in pharmaceuticals company Nycomed ASA fell on the Oslo bourse after the company posted lower than expected profits.
-The Central Bank is proposing a new law to give Norwegian bank more security in foreign exchange trade.
